{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# run_m2_full_starcoder_resume.sh — Resume 9 remaining runs (incl. BM25)
#
# random_s42 已完成 (step 4200/4242, checkpoints saved)
#   best_by_val_loss:    /root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/checkpoints/m2_full_starcoder/random_s42/best_by_val_loss/
#   best_by_recall_at_1: /root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/checkpoints/m2_full_starcoder/random_s42/best_by_recall_at_1/
#
# D026: s42 = 3 epochs, s43/s44 = 2 epochs
# ============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

PROJECT_ROOT="/root/structfuse"
MODEL_PATH="/root/autodl-tmp/models/bigcode/starcoder2-3b/bigcode/starcoder2-3b"
STARCODER_DATA_DIR="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_starcoder_data"
CHECKPOINT_BASE="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/checkpoints/m2_full_starcoder"
LOG_BASE="/root/runs/m2_full_starcoder"
BM25_DATA_DIR="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_training_data"
BM25_OUTPUT_BASE="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_outputs"

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

echo "============================================"
echo " StarCoder M2 Resume: 9 remaining runs"
echo " Start: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo " GPU: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
echo "============================================"

# (strategy, seed, epochs)
RUNS=(
    "random:43:2"
    "random:44:2"
    "bm25:42:3"
    "embedding_distance:42:3"
    "embedding_distance:43:2"
    "embedding_distance:44:2"
    "dataflow_aware:42:3"
    "dataflow_aware:43:2"
    "dataflow_aware:44:2"
)

mkdir -p "$LOG_BASE"

for run_spec in "${RUNS[@]}"; do
    IFS=':' read -r strategy seed epochs <<< "$run_spec"
    RUN_NAME="${strategy}_s${seed}"
    if [ "$strategy" = "bm25" ]; then
        OUTPUT_DIR="${BM25_OUTPUT_BASE}/bm25_starcoder_s${seed}"
        TRAIN_FILE="${BM25_DATA_DIR}/train_bm25_s${seed}.jsonl"
        VAL_FILE="${BM25_DATA_DIR}/val_bm25_s${seed}.jsonl"
    else
        OUTPUT_DIR="${CHECKPOINT_BASE}/${RUN_NAME}"
        TRAIN_FILE="${STARCODER_DATA_DIR}/train_${strategy}_s${seed}.jsonl"
        VAL_FILE="${STARCODER_DATA_DIR}/val_${strategy}_s${seed}.jsonl"
    fi
    RUN_LOG="${LOG_BASE}/${RUN_NAME}.log"

    echo ""
    echo "── Training: ${RUN_NAME} (${epochs} epochs) ──"
    echo "  Output: $OUTPUT_DIR"
    echo "  Log: $RUN_LOG"

    mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR" "$(dirname "$RUN_LOG")"

    EXTRA_ARGS=""
    if [ "$strategy" = "dataflow_aware" ] && [ -f "${STARCODER_DATA_DIR}/dataflow_graph.json" ]; then
        EXTRA_ARGS="--dataflow-graph-file ${STARCODER_DATA_DIR}/dataflow_graph.json"
    fi

    python -u "${PROJECT_ROOT}/training/train.py" \
        --model-name "$MODEL_PATH" \
        --train-file "$TRAIN_FILE" \
        --val-file "$VAL_FILE" \
        --output-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR" \
        --hard-negative-strategy "$strategy" \
        --seed "$seed" \
        --batch-size 8 \
        --num-negatives 7 \
        --max-seq-length 2048 \
        --num-epochs "$epochs" \
        --learning-rate 2e-5 \
        --temperature 0.07 \
        --hard-negative-ratio 0.5 \
        --eval-steps 500 \
        --save-steps 1000 \
        --use-lora \
        --gradient-checkpointing \
        --wandb-project structfuse \
        --wandb-run-name "m2_full_sc2_${RUN_NAME}" \
        --early-stopping-patience 2 \
        $EXTRA_ARGS \
        2>&1 | tee "$RUN_LOG"

    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] DONE: ${RUN_NAME}"

    if [ -d "${OUTPUT_DIR}/best" ]; then
        find "${OUTPUT_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name "checkpoint-*" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo " ALL 9 RESUME RUNS COMPLETED"
echo " End: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo "============================================"

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# run_m2_full_bm25_starcoder.sh — BM25 negative strategy Phase 2 training (StarCoder2-3B)
#
# Runs 3 seeds sequentially. Config matches other M2 strategies exactly,
# except: s42 uses 3 epochs; s43/s44 use 2 epochs + early_stopping_patience=2.
#
# NOTE: StarCoder2-3B model must be downloaded to MODEL_PATH before running.
#
# Usage:
#   nohup bash run_m2_full_bm25_starcoder.sh > /root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_outputs/bm25_starcoder_schedule.log 2>&1 &
# ============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_ROOT="/root/structfuse"
MODEL_PATH="/root/autodl-tmp/models/bigcode/starcoder2-3b/bigcode/starcoder2-3b"
DATA_DIR="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_training_data"
OUTPUT_BASE="/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_outputs"
GPU_ID="${1:-0}"

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$GPU_ID"
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Activate conda
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

# ── Seed configs: (seed, epochs, early_stopping_patience) ──
declare -a SEEDS=(42 43 44)
declare -A EPOCHS=([42]=3 [43]=2 [44]=2)
declare -A PATIENCE=([42]=0 [43]=2 [44]=2)

echo "============================================"
echo " BM25 StarCoder2-3B M2 Full Training"
echo " Seeds: ${SEEDS[*]}"
echo " GPU: $GPU_ID"
echo " Start: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo "============================================"

# Check model exists
if [ ! -e "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: StarCoder2-3B model not found at $MODEL_PATH"
    echo "Download it first: python -c \"from modelscope import snapshot_download; snapshot_download('AI-ModelScope/starcoder2-3b', cache_dir='/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/models')\""
    exit 1
fi

for SEED in "${SEEDS[@]}"; do
    STRATEGY="bm25"
    NUM_EPOCHS="${EPOCHS[$SEED]}"
    ESP="${PATIENCE[$SEED]}"
    OUTPUT_DIR="${OUTPUT_BASE}/bm25_starcoder_s${SEED}"
    TRAIN_FILE="${DATA_DIR}/train_bm25_s${SEED}.jsonl"
    VAL_FILE="${DATA_DIR}/val_bm25_s${SEED}.jsonl"
    LOG_FILE="${OUTPUT_DIR}/train.log"

    # Pre-flight checks
    for f in "$TRAIN_FILE" "$VAL_FILE"; do
        if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: required file not found: $f"
            exit 1
        fi
    done

    mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

    echo ""
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] START bm25_starcoder_s${SEED} (epochs=${NUM_EPOCHS}, patience=${ESP})"

    TRAIN_CMD=(
        python -u "${PROJECT_ROOT}/training/train.py"
        --model-name "$MODEL_PATH"
        --train-file "$TRAIN_FILE"
        --val-file "$VAL_FILE"
        --output-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR"
        --hard-negative-strategy "$STRATEGY"
        --seed "$SEED"
        --batch-size 8
        --num-negatives 7
        --max-seq-length 2048
        --num-epochs "$NUM_EPOCHS"
        --learning-rate 2e-5
        --eval-steps 500
        --save-steps 1000
        --use-lora
        --gradient-checkpointing
        --wandb-project structfuse
        --wandb-run-name "full_m2_bm25_starcoder_s${SEED}"
    )

    if [ "$ESP" -gt 0 ]; then
        TRAIN_CMD+=(--early-stopping-patience "$ESP")
    fi

    echo "CMD: ${TRAIN_CMD[*]}" | tee "$LOG_FILE"
    "${TRAIN_CMD[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"

    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] DONE bm25_starcoder_s${SEED}"
done

echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo " ALL BM25 STARCODER RUNS COMPLETED"
echo " End: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo "============================================"
", "stderr": "", "return_code": 0}, "error": null, "metadata": {"elapsed_seconds": 0.39}}

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# run_m2_s42_supplement.sh — M2 Full s42 补充训练
#
# 覆盖: embedding_distance_s42 + dataflow_aware_s42 (Qwen / StarCoder / both)
# D026: s42 使用 3 epochs, 无 early stopping, 提供完整 overfitting curve
# ============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ── Argument parsing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
GPU="cuda:0"
ENCODER="both"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --gpu)
            GPU="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --encoder)
            ENCODER="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        *)
            echo "ERROR: Unknown argument: $1"
            echo "Usage: $0 [--gpu cuda:N] [--encoder qwen|starcoder|both]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ "$ENCODER" != "qwen" && "$ENCODER" != "starcoder" && "$ENCODER" != "both" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: --encoder must be qwen, starcoder, or both (got: $ENCODER)"
    exit 1
fi

# ── Environment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_CONSOLE=off
export WANDB_DIR=/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/wandb_logs/
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

SEED=42
NUM_EPOCHS=3
STRATEGIES=("embedding_distance" "dataflow_aware")
TRAIN_SCRIPT="/root/structfuse/training/train.py"

echo "============================================"
echo " M2 Full s42 Supplement"
echo " Start: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo " GPU: ${GPU} (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-not set})"
echo " Encoder: ${ENCODER}"
echo " Strategies: ${STRATEGIES[*]}"
echo " Seed: ${SEED}, Epochs: ${NUM_EPOCHS}"
echo "============================================"

# ── Training function ────────────────────────────────────────────────
run_training() {
    local encoder_name="$1"
    local model_path="$2"
    local data_dir="$3"
    local out_base="$4"
    local log_dir="$5"
    local wandb_prefix="$6"

    mkdir -p "${log_dir}" "${out_base}"

    for STRATEGY in "${STRATEGIES[@]}"; do
        TAG="${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}"
        TRAIN_FILE="${data_dir}/train_${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}.jsonl"
        VAL_FILE="${data_dir}/val_${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}.jsonl"
        OUT_DIR="${out_base}/${TAG}"
        LOG_FILE="${log_dir}/${TAG}.log"

        echo ""
        echo "=========================================="
        echo " [${encoder_name}] ${TAG}"
        echo " Train: ${TRAIN_FILE}"
        echo " Output: ${OUT_DIR}"
        echo " Log: ${LOG_FILE}"
        echo "=========================================="

        if [ ! -f "${TRAIN_FILE}" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Train file not found: ${TRAIN_FILE}"
            exit 1
        fi
        if [ ! -f "${VAL_FILE}" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Val file not found: ${VAL_FILE}"
            exit 1
        fi

        mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}"

        EXTRA_ARGS=""
        if [ "${STRATEGY}" = "dataflow_aware" ]; then
            if [ -f "${data_dir}/dataflow_graph.json" ]; then
                EXTRA_ARGS="--dataflow-graph-file ${data_dir}/dataflow_graph.json"
            else
                echo "ERROR: dataflow_graph.json not found in ${data_dir}"
                exit 1
            fi
        fi

        python -u "${TRAIN_SCRIPT}" \
            --model-name "${model_path}" \
            --train-file "${TRAIN_FILE}" \
            --val-file "${VAL_FILE}" \
            --output-dir "${OUT_DIR}" \
            --hard-negative-strategy "${STRATEGY}" \
            --seed "${SEED}" \
            --batch-size 8 \
            --num-negatives 7 \
            --max-seq-length 2048 \
            --num-epochs "${NUM_EPOCHS}" \
            --learning-rate 2e-5 \
            --temperature 0.07 \
            --hard-negative-ratio 0.5 \
            --eval-steps 500 \
            --save-steps 1000 \
            --use-lora \
            --gradient-checkpointing \
            --wandb-project structfuse \
            --wandb-run-name "${wandb_prefix}_${TAG}" \

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# run_m2_s42_supplement.sh — M2 Full s42 补充训练
#
# 覆盖: embedding_distance_s42 + dataflow_aware_s42 (Qwen / StarCoder / both)
# D026: s42 使用 3 epochs, 无 early stopping, 提供完整 overfitting curve
# ============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ── Argument parsing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
GPU="cuda:0"
ENCODER="both"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --gpu)
            GPU="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --encoder)
            ENCODER="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        *)
            echo "ERROR: Unknown argument: $1"
            echo "Usage: $0 [--gpu cuda:N] [--encoder qwen|starcoder|both]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ "$ENCODER" != "qwen" && "$ENCODER" != "starcoder" && "$ENCODER" != "both" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: --encoder must be qwen, starcoder, or both (got: $ENCODER)"
    exit 1
fi

# ── Environment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_CONSOLE=off
export WANDB_DIR=/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/wandb_logs/
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

SEED=42
NUM_EPOCHS=3
STRATEGIES=("embedding_distance" "dataflow_aware")
TRAIN_SCRIPT="/root/structfuse/training/train.py"

echo "============================================"
echo " M2 Full s42 Supplement"
echo " Start: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo " GPU: ${GPU} (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-not set})"
echo " Encoder: ${ENCODER}"
echo " Strategies: ${STRATEGIES[*]}"
echo " Seed: ${SEED}, Epochs: ${NUM_EPOCHS}"
echo "============================================"

# ── Training function ────────────────────────────────────────────────
run_training() {
    local encoder_name="$1"
    local model_path="$2"
    local data_dir="$3"
    local out_base="$4"
    local log_dir="$5"
    local wandb_prefix="$6"

    mkdir -p "${log_dir}" "${out_base}"

    for STRATEGY in "${STRATEGIES[@]}"; do
        TAG="${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}"
        TRAIN_FILE="${data_dir}/train_${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}.jsonl"
        VAL_FILE="${data_dir}/val_${STRATEGY}_s${SEED}.jsonl"
        OUT_DIR="${out_base}/${TAG}"
        LOG_FILE="${log_dir}/${TAG}.log"

        echo ""
        echo "=========================================="
        echo " [${encoder_name}] ${TAG}"
        echo " Train: ${TRAIN_FILE}"
        echo " Output: ${OUT_DIR}"
        echo " Log: ${LOG_FILE}"
        echo "=========================================="

        if [ ! -f "${TRAIN_FILE}" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Train file not found: ${TRAIN_FILE}"
            exit 1
        fi
        if [ ! -f "${VAL_FILE}" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Val file not found: ${VAL_FILE}"
            exit 1
        fi

        mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}"

        EXTRA_ARGS=""
        if [ "${STRATEGY}" = "dataflow_aware" ]; then
            if [ -f "${data_dir}/dataflow_graph.json" ]; then
                EXTRA_ARGS="--dataflow-graph-file ${data_dir}/dataflow_graph.json"
            else
                echo "ERROR: dataflow_graph.json not found in ${data_dir}"
                exit 1
            fi
        fi

        python -u "${TRAIN_SCRIPT}" \
            --model-name "${model_path}" \
            --train-file "${TRAIN_FILE}" \
            --val-file "${VAL_FILE}" \
            --output-dir "${OUT_DIR}" \
            --hard-negative-strategy "${STRATEGY}" \
            --seed "${SEED}" \
            --batch-size 8 \
            --num-negatives 7 \
            --max-seq-length 2048 \
            --num-epochs "${NUM_EPOCHS}" \
            --learning-rate 2e-5 \
            --temperature 0.07 \
            --hard-negative-ratio 0.5 \
            --eval-steps 500 \
            --save-steps 1000 \
            --use-lora \
            --gradient-checkpointing \
            --wandb-project structfuse \
            --wandb-run-name "${wandb_prefix}_${TAG}" \
            ${EXTRA_ARGS} \
            2>&1 | tee "${LOG_FILE}"

        echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] DONE: ${encoder_name} ${TAG}"

        if [ -f "${OUT_DIR}/best_by_val_loss/training_config.json" ]; then
            echo "  best_by_val_loss checkpoint saved"
        fi
        if [ -f "${OUT_DIR}/best_by_recall_at_1/training_config.json" ]; then
            echo "  best_by_recall_at_1 checkpoint saved"
        fi

        find "${OUT_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name "checkpoint-*" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
        echo ""
    done
}

# ── Qwen ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$ENCODER" == "qwen" || "$ENCODER" == "both" ]]; then
    echo ""
    echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════╗"

fi

echo " End: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo "============================================"

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_5/projects/structfuse-context/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — StructFuse\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026\\n\\n## Core Claims (3)\\n\\n1. **True embedding-distance hard negative mining consistently improves contrastive code retrieval over random baselines, correcting the prior misconception that embedding negatives harm performance.** The reported \\\"harm\\\" (CoCoHaNeRe-derived, -27pp R@1) was an artifact of BM25-proxy negatives mislabeled as embedding-distance — genuine embedding mining yields +1.6–2.0pp R@1 across two decoder-only encoders with distinct pretraining corpora and representation geometries (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, StarCoder2-3B).\\n\\n2. **Structure-grounded (dataflow) hard negatives provide conditional additional benefit beyond embedding mining, mediated by encoder representation saturation.** When pretrained encoder representations are compressed (pos_sim > 0.98, as in Qwen), random and embedding negatives become too easy; dataflow-disconnected negatives force discrimination along a structural dimension the encoder cannot separate via text alone. When representation space is healthy (pos_sim ~ 0.80, as in StarCoder), embedding mining alone suffices. Mechanism: neg_difficulty margin analysis (+17% Qwen, +28% StarCoder) provides quantitative evidence for this interaction.\\n\\n3. **Scope-bounded inter-procedural data-flow analysis via CodeQL provides a practical pipeline for computing structural connectivity at scale.** 0% timeout, 78% connected-not-gold rate (Z%), 123/131 repos with output at full scale. [Dream [M][W] flag: this is supporting methodology, not a primary research contribution. Drop speculative generalization claims (molecular networks, etc.) — no evidence. Frame as practical tool that enables the study, not a standalone contribution.]\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: Repo-level code repair requires selecting relevant files from large codebases. Current retrievers rely on text similarity alone, but lexical similarity ≠ structural relevance. Hard negative mining is the standard approach to improve contrastive retrievers, yet the field lacks systematic understanding of what negative selection strategies work for code and why.\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**:\\n  - Text-based retrieval (SweRank, SWE-Fixer): blind to structural dependencies\\n  - Graph-guided at inference (LocAgent, RANGER, CodexGraph): structural graphs at inference only, no training signal\\n  - ARISE: data-flow but intra-procedural only (no call boundary crossing), runtime tool calls only\\n  - CoCoHaNeRe: reports embedding negatives harm code search — but uses BM25 proxy, not true embedding distance\\n  - Gap: no systematic study comparing negative mining strategies with proper controls, and no mechanistic explanation for when/why each strategy works\\n\\n- **Our contribution**: A systematic analysis of hard negative mining strategies for contrastive code retrieval. We (1) correct the misconception that embedding negatives harm performance (BM25 proxy ≠ embedding distance), (2) introduce structure-grounded negatives via inter-procedural dataflow and characterize when they provide additional benefit, and (3) provide mechanistic explanation via representation space saturation analysis.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"True embedding-distance mining consistently improves code retrieval (+1.6–2.0pp R@1, 2 encoders), correcting prior reports of harm. Structure-grounded (dataflow) negatives provide further conditional benefit (+0.8–2.3pp) when encoder representations are saturated, with the interaction mechanism quantified via negative difficulty analysis.\\\"\\n\\n## Core Insight\\n\\nThe effectiveness of hard negative mining strategies depends on the encoder's representation geometry. When the pretrained space is saturated (high pos_sim → low margin between positive and negative), the encoder needs harder negatives from an orthogonal signal dimension (structure). When the space has healthy separation, embedding-distance mining alone captures sufficient difficulty gradient. This encoder-strategy interaction explains contradictory findings in prior work.\\n\\n## Dual-Pillar Motivation\\n\\n1. **Primary — Systematic analysis correcting misconceptions**: Prior work (CoCoHaNeRe) conflated BM25-proxy negatives with true embedding-distance negatives, leading to incorrect conclusions about hard negative mining for code. Our controlled comparison isolates the effect of each strategy.\\n2. **Secondary — Mechanistic explanation via representation geometry**: neg_difficulty analysis (margin distribution × strategy × encoder) provides explanatory depth beyond empirical comparison, enabling practitioners to predict which strategy suits their encoder without exhaustive experiments.\\n\\n## Formal Definition\\n\\nGiven retrieval domain D, structural graph G, similarity function s, query q:\\n**structure-grounded hard negative** = argmax_{x ∈ D : s(x,q) > τ ∧ ¬reachable_G(x,q)} s(x,q)\\n\\nThe structural graph is externally fixed and does not update with the encoder (drift-immune).\\n\\n## Title Options\\n\\n- Primary: \\\"What Makes Hard Negatives Work for Code Retrieval? A Systematic Study of Mining Strategies and Representation Geometry\\\"\\n- Alternative: \\\"StructFuse: When and Why Structure-Grounded Hard Negatives Improve Contrastive Code Retrieval\\\"\\n- Backup: \\\"Correcting Misconceptions in Hard Negative Mining for Code: Embedding Distance Helps, Structure Helps Conditionally\\\"\\n\\n## Venue Fit\\n\\n1. **EMNLP Main fit**: Empirical analysis + mechanistic insight papers are a strong EMNLP archetype (cf. \\\"Do Language Models...\\\" papers). Contribution is understanding, not just a new method.\\n2. **NLP audience**: Frame as contrastive learning methodology with code as instantiation. Representation geometry analysis generalizes beyond code.\\n3. **Against \\\"incremental\\\" criticism**: Paper corrects a misconception + provides mechanistic explanation + introduces new negative mining paradigm. Three contributions, not one marginal improvement.\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n| Concern | Response | Evidence |\\n|---------|----------|----------|\\n| Only 2 encoders — can you generalize? | n=2 is minimum for interaction claim; we frame as observation with mechanism, not universal law; two decoder-only encoders with distinct pretraining (Fill vs FIM) and representation geometry (pos_sim 0.99 vs 0.80) provide meaningful variation | plan_013 (done), m2_full runs |\\n| BM25 vs true embedding negatives? | Run BM25 negatives to empirically verify CoCoHaNeRe used BM25-proxy, closing the correction argument | plan_018 |\\n| Pool size sensitivity? | Evaluate at pool {50, 100, 200, 500} to confirm strategy rankings hold at realistic sizes | plan_019 |\\n| Stratified by structural data availability? | Report per-stratum R@1 for 34% with structural data vs 66% fallback | plan_005 (extended) |\\n| Temperature regime specificity | Ablate τ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} | plan_014 |\\n| No downstream task evaluation | SWE-bench Lite end-to-end with LLM agent | plan_003 |\\n| Static vs dynamic mining confound | Clarify mining is static; add dynamic baseline | plan_015 |\\n| CodeQL scalability at larger scale | 0% timeout, 78% Z%, 123 repos; m1_reextract_v2 adds more | plan_006 (done) |\\n| Why not compare inference-time graph methods? | Complementary: they navigate at inference, we mine at training. Discuss relationship. | plan_017 |\\n| Single benchmark | Add RepoBench-R cross-file retrieval | plan_004 |\\n| Statistical significance | Bootstrap 95% CI for all comparisons; full M2 = 9 seeds × 3 strategies × 2 encoders | plan_016, m2_full |\\n| \\\"Complementary signal\\\" overstatement | Temper: \\\"conditionally beneficial\\\" not \\\"always complementary\\\" | Writing discipline |\\n| Missing related work | RepoFusion, GRACE, GraphCodeBERT, ANCE, curriculum HN mining | Writing task |\\n\\n## Evidence Status\\n\\n### Confirmed findings (basis for claims):\\n- D017: True embedding mining helps (+2.0pp Qwen, +1.6pp StarCoder) — corrects MVP BM25-proxy artifact\\n- D021/neg_difficulty: Qwen pos_sim=0.9855 (saturated), StarCoder pos_sim=0.7985 (healthy); margin differential explains strategy interaction\\n- m2_embed_verify (pilot): 3-strategy comparison confirms ranking (embedding > random, dataflow conditional)\\n- plan_013 (StarCoder pilot): Confirms cross-encoder pattern — embedding helps both, dataflow helps Qwen only\\n- plan_006: CodeQL scalability confirmed at 123-repo scale\\n\\n### In progress:\\n- m2_full_qwen: 9 seeds × 3 strategies (seed 1 running, best R@1=55.3% at step 1000)\\n- m2_full_starcoder: 9 seeds × 3 strategies (seed 1 running, R@1=45.4% at step 1000, still improving)\\n- m1_reextract_v2: expanded extraction for higher coverage\\n\\n### Planned (priority order):\\n- plan_018: BM25 negative baseline (Dream #1 consensus gap — closes CoCoHaNeRe correction argument)\\n- plan_003: SWE-bench Lite eval (biggest lever for paper strength)\\n- plan_019: Pool size sensitivity (Dream consensus — external validity)\\n- plan_014: Temperature ablation (Dream reviewer concern)\\n- plan_004: RepoBench-R second benchmark (with multi-seed CIs)\\n- plan_015: Dynamic mining baseline\\n- plan_005: Stratified analysis (extended: structural-available vs fallback stratum)\\n- plan_007/008/009: Additional ablations\\n\\n## Contingency (if full M2 results weaken claims)\\n\\n### All 18 runs confirm pilot pattern: Best case\\n- Full statistical power, paper as framed above\\n- Target: EMNLP Main\\n\\n### Dataflow benefit disappears even for Qwen at full scale: Pivot to 2-claim paper\\n- Drop Claim 2 to analysis observation\\n- Paper becomes: \\\"True embedding mining helps (correcting misconception) + CodeQL extraction is practical + representation geometry analysis explains prior contradictions\\\"\\n- Still publishable: correcting misconception + mechanistic analysis is sufficient for EMNLP Main\\n\\n### BM25 negatives ≈ random (not harmful): Narrative pivot needed [D030 contingency]\\n- If plan_018 shows BM25 negatives perform ≈ random (not << random), the \\\"correcting misconception\\\" narrative loses empirical anchor\\n- Pivot: from \\\"CoCoHaNeRe was wrong because BM25 proxy\\\" → \\\"systematic comparison reveals embedding-distance mining is the only strategy that consistently helps; prior work's negative finding was likely due to uncontrolled variables (data, training protocol), not BM25 specifically\\\"\\n- Paper becomes less dramatic (\\\"correcting\\\" → \\\"clarifying\\\") but still valid as systematic analysis\\n- Claim 1 reworded: \\\"True embedding-distance mining consistently improves code retrieval\\\" (drop the \\\"correcting misconception\\\" framing, keep the empirical finding)\\n- Impact: weaker narrative hook but core experimental contribution survives\\n\\n### Embedding mining also loses advantage at full scale: Major reassessment needed\\n- Recheck data pipeline for bugs (full-scale data may have distribution differences)\\n- If confirmed: negative result paper — \\\"Why Hard Negative Mining Doesn't Scale for Code Retrieval\\\"\\n- Discuss with user before committing direction\\n\\n## Deprecated Claims (with reason)\\n\\n- ~~\\\"Embedding-distance hard negatives actively harm code retrieval\\\"~~ — FALSIFIED by D017. Original evidence (-27pp R@1) was from BM25-proxy negatives incorrectly labeled as embedding_distance in MVP. True embedding mining shows consistent improvement. Preserved here to prevent regression.\\n\", \"total_chars\": 11181, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main
- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026

## Core Claims (3)

1. **True embedding-distance hard negative mining consistently improves contrastive code retrieval over random baselines, correcting the prior misconception that embedding negatives harm performance.** The reported "harm" (CoCoHaNeRe-derived, -27pp R@1) was an artifact of BM25-proxy negatives mislabeled as embedding-distance — genuine embedding mining yields +1.6–2.0pp R@1 across two decoder-only encoders with distinct pretraining corpora and representation geometries (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, StarCoder2-3B).

2. **Structure-grounded (dataflow) hard negatives provide conditional additional benefit beyond embedding mining, mediated by encoder representation saturation.** When pretrained encoder representations are compressed (pos_sim > 0.98, as in Qwen), random and embedding negatives become too easy; dataflow-disconnected negatives force discrimination along a structural dimension the encoder cannot separate via text alone. When representation space is healthy (pos_sim ~ 0.80, as in StarCoder), embedding mining alone suffices. Mechanism: neg_difficulty margin analysis (+17% Qwen, +28% StarCoder) provides quantitative evidence for this interaction.

3. **Scope-bounded inter-procedural data-flow analysis via CodeQL provides a practical pipeline for computing structural connectivity at scale.** 0% timeout, 78% connected-not-gold rate (Z%), 123/131 repos with output at full scale. [Dream [M][W] flag: this is supporting methodology, not a primary research contribution. Drop speculative generalization claims (molecular networks, etc.) — no evidence. Frame as practical tool that enables the study, not a standalone contribution.]

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Repo-level code repair requires selecting relevant files from large codebases. Current retrievers rely on text similarity alone, but lexical similarity ≠ structural relevance. Hard negative mining is the standard approach to improve contrastive retrievers, yet the field lacks systematic understanding of what negative selection strategies work for code and why.

- **Existing approaches & gaps**:
  - Text-based retrieval (SweRank, SWE-Fixer): blind to structural dependencies
  - Graph-guided at inference (LocAgent, RANGER, CodexGraph): structural graphs at inference only, no training signal
  - ARISE: data-flow but intra-procedural only (no call boundary crossing), runtime tool calls only
  - CoCoHaNeRe: reports embedding negatives harm code search — but uses BM25 proxy, not true embedding distance
  - Gap: no systematic study comparing negative mining strategies with proper controls, and no mechanistic explanation for when/why each strategy works

- **Our contribution**: A systematic analysis of hard negative mining strategies for contrastive code retrieval. We (1) correct the misconception that embedding negatives harm performance (BM25 proxy ≠ embedding distance), (2) introduce structure-grounded negatives via inter-procedural dataflow and characterize when they provide additional benefit, and (3) provide mechanistic explanation via representation space saturation analysis.

- **Headline result template**: "True embedding-distance mining consistently improves code retrieval (+1.6–2.0pp R@1, 2 encoders), correcting prior reports of harm. Structure-grounded (dataflow) negatives provide further conditional benefit (+0.8–2.3pp) when encoder representations are saturated, with the interaction mechanism quantified via negative difficulty analysis."

## Core Insight

The effectiveness of hard negative mining strategies depends on the encoder's representation geometry. When the pretrained space is saturated (high pos_sim → low margin between positive and negative), the encoder needs harder negatives from an orthogonal signal dimension (structure). When the space has healthy separation, embedding-distance mining alone captures sufficient difficulty gradient. This encoder-strategy interaction explains contradictory findings in prior work.

## Dual-Pillar Motivation

1. **Primary — Systematic analysis correcting misconceptions**: Prior work (CoCoHaNeRe) conflated BM25-proxy negatives with true embedding-distance negatives, leading to incorrect conclusions about hard negative mining for code. Our controlled comparison isolates the effect of each strategy.
2. **Secondary — Mechanistic explanation via representation geometry**: neg_difficulty analysis (margin distribution × strategy × encoder) provides explanatory depth beyond empirical comparison, enabling practitioners to predict which strategy suits their encoder without exhaustive experiments.

## Formal Definition

Given retrieval domain D, structural graph G, similarity function s, query q:
**structure-grounded hard negative** = argmax_{x ∈ D : s(x,q) > τ ∧ ¬reachable_G(x,q)} s(x,q)

The structural graph is externally fixed and does not update with the encoder (drift-immune).

## Title Options

- Primary: "What Makes Hard Negatives Work for Code Retrieval? A Systematic Study of Mining Strategies and Representation Geometry"
- Alternative: "StructFuse: When and Why Structure-Grounded Hard Negatives Improve Contrastive Code Retrieval"
- Backup: "Correcting Misconceptions in Hard Negative Mining for Code: Embedding Distance Helps, Structure Helps Conditionally"

## Venue Fit

1. **EMNLP Main fit**: Empirical analysis + mechanistic insight papers are a strong EMNLP archetype (cf. "Do Language Models..." papers). Contribution is understanding, not just a new method.
2. **NLP audience**: Frame as contrastive learning methodology with code as instantiation. Representation geometry analysis generalizes beyond code.
3. **Against "incremental" criticism**: Paper corrects a misconception + provides mechanistic explanation + introduces new negative mining paradigm. Three contributions, not one marginal improvement.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

| Concern | Response | Evidence |
|---------|----------|----------|
| Only 2 encoders — can you generalize? | n=2 is minimum for interaction claim; we frame as observation with mechanism, not universal law; two decoder-only encoders with distinct pretraining (Fill vs FIM) and representation geometry (pos_sim 0.99 vs 0.80) provide meaningful variation | plan_013 (done), m2_full runs |
| BM25 vs true embedding negatives? | Run BM25 negatives to empirically verify CoCoHaNeRe used BM25-proxy, closing the correction argument | plan_018 |
| Pool size sensitivity? | Evaluate at pool {50, 100, 200, 500} to confirm strategy rankings hold at realistic sizes | plan_019 |
| Stratified by structural data availability? | Report per-stratum R@1 for 34% with structural data vs 66% fallback | plan_005 (extended) |
| Temperature regime specificity | Ablate τ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} | plan_014 |
| No downstream task evaluation | SWE-bench Lite end-to-end with LLM agent | plan_003 |
| Static vs dynamic mining confound | Clarify mining is static; add dynamic baseline | plan_015 |
| CodeQL scalability at larger scale | 0% timeout, 78% Z%, 123 repos; m1_reextract_v2 adds more | plan_006 (done) |
| Why not compare inference-time graph methods? | Complementary: they navigate at inference, we mine at training. Discuss relationship. | plan_017 |
| Single benchmark | Add RepoBench-R cross-file retrieval | plan_004 |
| Statistical significance | Bootstrap 95% CI for all comparisons; full M2 = 9 seeds × 3 strategies × 2 encoders | plan_016, m2_full |
| "Complementary signal" overstatement | Temper: "conditionally beneficial" not "always complementary" | Writing discipline |
| Missing related work | RepoFusion, GRACE, GraphCodeBERT, ANCE, curriculum HN mining | Writing task |

## Evidence Status

### Confirmed findings (basis for claims):
- D017: True embedding mining helps (+2.0pp Qwen, +1.6pp StarCoder) — corrects MVP BM25-proxy artifact
- D021/neg_difficulty: Qwen pos_sim=0.9855 (saturated), StarCoder pos_sim=0.7985 (healthy); margin differential explains strategy interaction
- m2_embed_verify (pilot): 3-strategy comparison confirms ranking (embedding > random, dataflow conditional)
- plan_013 (StarCoder pilot): Confirms cross-encoder pattern — embedding helps both, dataflow helps Qwen only
- plan_006: CodeQL scalability confirmed at 123-repo scale

### In progress:
- m2_full_qwen: 9 seeds × 3 strategies (seed 1 running, best R@1=55.3% at step 1000)
- m2_full_starcoder: 9 seeds × 3 strategies (seed 1 running, R@1=45.4% at step 1000, still improving)
- m1_reextract_v2: expanded extraction for higher coverage

- plan_014: Temperature ablation (Dream reviewer concern)
- plan_004: RepoBench-R second benchmark (with multi-seed CIs)

- Full statistical power, paper as framed above
- Target: EMNLP Main

- Drop Claim 2 to analysis observation
- Paper becomes: "True embedding mining helps (correcting misconception) + CodeQL extraction is practical + representation geometry analysis explains prior contradictions"

- Impact: weaker narrative hook but core experimental contribution survives

- Discuss with user before committing direction
